description: What the remote app may ask of the shell. The app is the deployed origin, not bundled code, so it is granted exactly what a browser tab could not do for itself and nothing a tab already can. The updater, the process plugin, the store, autostart, deep-link and the shell's opener are deliberately absent: the shell updates itself from Rust, owns its own tray settings, and exposes three narrow commands, so a page that runs somebody else's script cannot make this process install software, restart itself, register a URL scheme, start with the machine, or hand a URL of any scheme to the operating system. The three `allow-*` entries at the end are the shell's own commands: an app command reaching this window from a REMOTE origin is refused unless it is named here AND in build.rs's app manifest, with no error at build time and a rejected promise the bridge reads as 'no shell' — which is how the badge and the link opener were dead for a release without anybody noticing.
